title: Unspecified Need
text: 2:14 AM. "{ME}. I need you." You're there in eleven seconds. "What do you need?" A long pause in the dark. "...I don't know."

choices.label: Go through every need, alphabetically

outcomes.text: Blanket? No. Bun-Bun? No. Cup? No. Door open? No. "Elbow?" An elbow comes out from under the blanket. You hold the elbow until 2:40.
You get as far as "water" before they're asleep. It might have been water. You finish the alphabet in your head out of spite. There's nothing for Q.

choices.label: Lie on the floor until they figure it out

outcomes.text: You wake at 4:10 on the rug with a puzzle piece stuck to your cheek. They're asleep. Whatever they needed, it was you, horizontal.

choices.label: "Ask {partner}. {partner} knows."

outcomes.text: {partner} goes in. Twenty minutes later they lie back down without a word. "What did they need?" "I don't know," they say. "But I gave it to them."
"They said {me}," {partner} says, without opening their eyes. "I heard it." Correct, and unbearable. You go back in.

title: The Performance
text: 3:03 AM. Crying. Beside you, {partner}'s breathing switches from asleep to performing asleep. You know the difference. You've given that performance.

choices.label: Out-sleep them. Commit fully.

outcomes.text: Nine minutes of competitive sleeping. {partner} cracks first, lets out a sigh with paragraphs in it and gets up. You stay limp until the door closes, to sell it.
Neither of you breaks. The crying stops on its own at 3:12. You both lie there in the dark, knowing exactly what the other one did.
"Nobody breathes that evenly," {partner} whispers. "Not even asleep." Betrayed by your own lungs. You go.

choices.label: Whisper, "I know you're awake."

outcomes.text: "I know you know," {partner} whispers. A long pause. "...Fine." They go. The ledger remains undefeated.
"And I know what the ledger says," {partner} whispers back. So do you. You go.

choices.label: Get up. Sigh loud enough to go on the record.

outcomes.text: You sigh at a volume that will come up in future arguments. {partner} says, "Thank you," which ruins it, because now you can't be mad.

title: Was There a One?
text: 3:31 AM. Crying again. "I got up at one," {partner} whispers. You have no memory of one. You're not sure one happened. You're not sure this is happening.

choices.label: "Prove it."

outcomes.text: {partner} thinks about it for a long time. "...I might have dreamed one." They get up. Somewhere, one o'clock is laughing at both of you.
They describe one in detail: the rabbit, the wet sock, you snoring through all of it. One happened. You go.

choices.label: "I ALSO got up at one."

outcomes.text: "...Oh," says {partner}, thrown. You both lie there wondering if one o'clock had two of you in it. They get up, just in case.
"At one you were asleep with your mouth open," {partner} whispers. "I took a photo." They have a photo. You go.

choices.label: Just go. Nobody can be trusted at 3:31.

outcomes.text: You go. They're asleep before you get there. You stand in the hallway at 3:40 trying to remember one. You remember a sock.

title: Phantom Cry
text: You're standing next to the crib. {kid} is asleep. You don't remember getting up. You don't know if they called, or if your body just went without you.

choices.label: Check the monitor app for evidence

outcomes.text: Last sound detected: 11:42 PM. Nobody called. Your body is volunteering now, like an intern who really wants the job.

choices.label: Stay a minute. Watch them breathe.

outcomes.text: One hand on the rail. Their back goes up and down, up and down. You stay ten minutes for no reason, and it's the best reason you've had all week.
Their eyes open. They look at you, say "Hi" at a normal volume, and are asleep again before you can answer. You'll never know if that counted.

choices.label: Claim it on the ledger anyway

outcomes.text: "Thanks for getting it," {partner} mumbles. You accept the credit. You did get up. Technically, for someone.
"The monitor didn't go off," {partner} mumbles. "I'd have heard it." They wouldn't have. But they're right.

title: The Dream Report
text: 1:50 AM. On the monitor, {kid} says, clearly, fast asleep: "No. That's not how you do it." A pause. Then, deeply disappointed in someone: "Watch me."

choices.label: Lie there and listen. Best show you get.

outcomes.text: "...and THEN the duck," they explain to someone. "NO. The OTHER duck." Then snoring. You'll think about the other duck all day.
The dream turns into an argument, and the argument turns into a scream. You lose the show and get the encore.

choices.label: Wake {partner}. Nobody should hear this alone.

outcomes.text: "Watch me," says the monitor, again. {partner} laughs into the pillow so hard the bed shakes. You haven't laughed together at 2 AM since before. You should do this more.
"Why," {partner} says, flatly, at 1:52 AM. The monitor has gone silent. You have woken an adult to listen to nothing.

choices.label: Go in and see who they're mad at

outcomes.text: The door creaks. {kid} sits straight up, wide awake and furious. Whoever they were mad at in the dream, it's you now.

title: Fourteen Inches
text: {kid} is asleep between you. Nobody can move. Nobody can speak. {partner} texts you from fourteen inches away.

messages.text: thats their foot. its in my ribs

choices.label: "rock paper scissors. in the dark. go"

outcomes.text: You throw rock. They throw something you can't see and claim it was paper. You can't prove it. You carry {kid} back.
You throw paper and whisper "paper." They concede. The mattress shifts as they lift {kid} like a cake with the candles already lit.

choices.label: "leave them. we live like this now"

outcomes.text: You sleep on nine inches of mattress. You wake at 5 with a heel in your ear and a hand on your face. You'll be sore all day. You won't mind.

choices.label: carry them back yourself. no notes.

outcomes.text: A flawless transfer. They don't stir. You get back into a bed that is suddenly enormous.
Halfway down the hall they open their eyes, see the hallway and understand everything. The scream wakes the neighbor's dog.

title: The Ocean Stops
text: 3:10 AM. The sound machine's ocean cuts out. The silence is so loud that {kid} sits up to find out what happened to the ocean.

choices.label: Be the ocean. "Shhhhhhhhhhhhh."

outcomes.text: You shush for nineteen straight minutes. They lie back down. You're lightheaded and slightly blue, but you're a coastline now.
{kid} listens to your ocean, unimpressed. "No. The REAL ocean." Your ocean has been reviewed.

choices.label: Find the plug in the dark by feel

outcomes.text: You find a plug. You push it in. The ocean comes back mid-wave, like it never left. Nobody will ever know you did that.
You find a plug. You push it in. It's the lamp. Sixty watts, straight into the face of a toddler who was 80% asleep.

choices.label: Nudge {partner}: "The ocean's down."

outcomes.text: "On it," {partner} mumbles, as if the ocean were a server. It's back up in ninety seconds. Nobody files a ticket.
"You bought it," {partner} says into the pillow. "You support it." Brutal, but that's the policy. You go.

title: "Is It Morning?"
text: 4:52 AM. A bright little voice: "Is it morning?" It is not morning. It's a number. They're standing in the crib holding one of your shoes. You don't know how they got a shoe.

choices.label: "It's still night." Repeat until true.

outcomes.text: You say it nine times in the same flat voice, like a gate agent. On the tenth, they lie down. You don't. Your body has clocked in.
On the eleventh "it's still night," a bird starts singing. {kid} points at the window, triumphant. The bird has testified against you.

choices.label: Say "your turn" into the pillow

outcomes.text: {partner} goes without a word. At 5:01 you hear them downstairs, whispering a book about diggers, doing every digger's voice. You fall asleep to the excavator.
"Your turn for mornings," {partner} says into their pillow. Is it? Neither of you can remember who has mornings. You go. You come back holding the shoe.

choices.label: Pretend to be asleep. Commit fully.

outcomes.text: It works. They talk quietly to the shoe for twenty minutes and fall back asleep holding it. Some questions answer themselves.
"Is it morning?" becomes "IT'S MORNING," which is not a question. It is now, technically, morning.

title: Trained
text: 4:02 AM. Nothing has happened all night. You and {partner} wake up at the exact same second anyway, both grab for the monitor, and stare at a sleeping child. You've both been trained.

choices.label: Put it down. Don't jinx it.

outcomes.text: You both lie back down without a word. Neither of you says "we got a whole night" out loud, because you're not amateurs.
You lie back down. {partner} whispers, "We did it. A whole night." From the monitor, very small: "{ME}?"

choices.label: Watch them sleep for a minute. Together.

outcomes.text: Two adults and one glowing screen, watching someone 34 inches long breathe. Nobody says anything. Nobody has to.

choices.label: Go check in person. Just to be sure.

outcomes.text: The floorboard outside their door has one job. It does it. {kid} sits up and says, "Is it breakfast?"
You make it to the door, look in and make it back without a creak. You've never been so quiet in your life. Nobody will ever know.

title: The Replay
text: 3:12 AM. You're replaying the moment you lost it today. In the replay you're calm. In the replay you crouch down to their level. In real life, you didn't.

choices.label: Wake {partner} and say it out loud

outcomes.text: They listen with their eyes closed. "You're a good parent having a hard week," they mumble. "Those aren't opposites." It helps more than it should.

choices.label: Plan tomorrow's sorry

outcomes.text: Get down to their level. Say what happened. Say it wasn't okay. Say you love them. You run it three times and fall asleep on the second "I love you."

choices.label: Go stand in their doorway

outcomes.text: They're asleep on their back, arms flung up, the way they sleep when they feel safe. Tomorrow you'll say sorry. They'll say "okay" and ask for a snack. That's what repair looks like at two.

title: Live From the Crib
text: 11:48 PM. The toddler who wasn't sleepy at bedtime is now hosting a late-night show from the crib. Tonight's guests: Bun-Bun and a sock. The monologue is the word "BUS."

choices.label: Be the dullest guest in TV history

outcomes.text: You sit in the dark and read the sound machine's warranty aloud, in a monotone. By "limitation of liability," the show is over. Your best set ever, and nobody laughed.

choices.label: Book {partner} as the closing act

outcomes.text: {partner} goes in and does the slow-blink-and-hum thing they're weirdly good at. The show is cancelled in six minutes. Network decision.
"You did bedtime," {partner} whispers. "This is your encore." Harsh. Accurate. You go in to a standing ovation from one.

choices.label: Let the show run long

outcomes.text: The show runs until 12:31 and ends in the middle of "BUS." They fell asleep on air.
The show gets picked up for a second season. At 1:05 you go in, and they greet you like a superfan who got backstage.

title: The Fridge Is Thinking
text: 1:30 AM. Everyone in the house is asleep but you. You can hear the fridge thinking. You can hear your own eyelids. The 4 PM coffee is still at work.

choices.label: You're up anyway. Take the next shift.

outcomes.text: At 2:10 the monitor crackles and you're there in nine seconds, because you were already standing at the door. {partner} wakes up suspiciously rested.

choices.label: Reorganize the snack drawer by feel

outcomes.text: You sort 31 snacks by crunch, in total darkness. In the morning, {partner} opens the drawer, looks at it for a while and quietly closes it again.

choices.label: Catch up on the group chat at 1% brightness

outcomes.text: You vote in the pajama-day poll and answer a six-day-old bake sale question. At 1:34 AM someone replies, "are you ok?"
You scroll so far back you accidentally heart a photo from 2022. Everyone gets the notification. At 1:36 AM, Brynn hearts your heart.

title: The Molar, Live
text: 1:15 AM. The molar is still coming in, and it wants everyone to know. {kid} is gnawing the crib rail and crying in a key you didn't know existed.

choices.label: Rocking chair. Cold washcloth. The long haul.

outcomes.text: Forty minutes in the chair. They chew the washcloth, then your sleeve, then your thumb, then fall asleep mid-chew. You know exactly where the molar is now. So does your thumb.
Twenty minutes in, they fall asleep on your shoulder with their mouth open, slowly soaking your shirt. You stay another twenty anyway.

choices.label: Read the dose chart twice. Measure once.

outcomes.text: Kitchen light on. You read the chart twice and measure with the syringe, not a spoon. Twenty minutes later the crying winds down to a hum.

choices.label: Tag {partner}: "Tooth shift's yours."

outcomes.text: {partner} takes it. Through the wall you hear them make up a song about the tooth. Verse three rhymes "molar" with "polar bear." It's working.
"I did the last molar," {partner} whispers. There have been four molars. You decide not to audit this at 1 AM. You go.

title: 3 AM: Key Change
text: 3:02 AM. Nobody is crying. Nobody needs anything. You're awake because the Sunshine Sing-Along theme is playing in your head at full volume, key change and all.

choices.label: Hum it once. Exorcise it.

outcomes.text: You hum one bar. Still asleep, {partner} hums the harmony. You lie there in the dark, a duet nobody asked for.
You hum one bar. Through the monitor, a small voice picks up the next one. Now it's a concert, and you're the opening act.

choices.label: Put in one earbud. Rain sounds.

outcomes.text: Real rain, recorded somewhere with weather. You're asleep by 3:15, smiling.
The rain is lovely for four minutes. Then your brain finds the beat and lays the theme song over it. It's a remix now. It's better. That's the problem.

choices.label: Wake {partner}: "Do you have it too?"

outcomes.text: "I've had it since last week," they whisper. "I didn't want to give it to you." The most romantic thing anyone has ever said to you.
"I do now," {partner} says, bitterly, at 3:04 AM. You've passed it on. You fall asleep in a minute, free.

title: The 3 AM Agenda
text: 3:07 AM. Your brain has called a meeting. Attendance is mandatory. The agenda is everything you said "later" to this week, read aloud, in order.

choices.label: Do the oldest thing on the list. Now. One thumb.

outcomes.text: You do it in the dark at 4% brightness, with one thumb. Confirmation email: 3:22 AM. The meeting is adjourned. You are now, unfortunately, awake.

choices.label: Write it on your hand in the dark

outcomes.text: In the morning your hand says "THE THING" in ballpoint. It works. You do the thing before breakfast, still a little proud of the handwriting.
In the morning your hand says "THE THING" in ballpoint. You stare at it on and off all day, like a riddle you left yourself.

choices.label: Table it. Future you can handle it.

outcomes.text: Future you has been handling everything since March. Future you is so tired of you. You fall asleep anyway.

title: Grandma Has It
text: 2:20 AM. Crying. Before either of you moves, the guest-room door opens. Slippers in the hall. Then Grandma, in the nursery, singing a song you haven't heard since you were four.

choices.label: Let Grandma win this one

outcomes.text: The crying stops in three minutes. At breakfast Grandma says, "They sleep fine for me," butters toast like someone who has won an argument, and posts about it by 8.

choices.label: Sit in the hallway. Be four again.

outcomes.text: It's the song about the little boat. You forgot you knew it. You hum the second verse in the dark hallway, very quietly, so nobody hears.

choices.label: Go in. Your kid, your shift.

outcomes.text: "I've got it," Grandma whispers. "I've got it," you whisper back. Two grown adults whisper "I've got it" over a crib until {kid} falls asleep out of boredom.
